title: Make the empty collar catch the landing light
where: landing(), inside the scene===5 block, after its collar line and before the outer ctx.restore()
goal: The headless coat stays dark, but the two lapels and the seam beneath its empty collar are readable on a phone. These marks move with the existing slow breath, not independently.

title: Give the familiar coat a worn cuff and seam
where: coat(), after its existing fold lines (outside the shadow save/restore)
goal: A pair of warm worn cuffs gives the coat a recognizable detail at home, on the landing and in the second ending. The same helper draws all appearances; the detail is a visual rhyme, not a new clue or line of story.

title: Leave two scratches beside the missing coat
where: hook(), after its existing curved-hook stroke
goal: The bare hook is a place with wear, not an isolated symbol. The same two tiny scratches appear beside it at home and in the ending's glimpse into the flat, helping the visitor recognize which side they are on.

title: Let the hem under the door catch a little light
where: hallway(), inside scene===4, after the two existing hem fold lines
goal: The hem is visibly cloth, with one continuous uneven lit edge rather than an indistinct dark patch. Its existing outline and folds stay unchanged; it does not move or reach toward the player.

title: Show the chain shadow crossing a slit of door light
where: hallway(), in scene===6's chain-shadow else branch, BEFORE the loop of twelve dark chain links
goal: The taut chain links have a small lit floor to cast their shadow on. The impossible change of sides is easier to read; the light remains steady and local, not an echo pulse or screen flash.

title: Carry a strip of hall light onto the outside landing
where: outside(), immediately after the cracked-door wall wedge polygon and BEFORE that wedge's clip/save block
goal: The cracked door lights a narrow threshold on the landing. This makes the final reversal feel like a physical place connected to the familiar hall, without adding an explanatory caption.

title: Separate the two empty collars in the open doorway
where: welcome(), inside its two-coat for loop AFTER each empty-collar ellipse fill
goal: Both collars can be counted in the dark wedge, even though the coats still overlap. It remains a cramped doorway and a quiet ending, not two bright figures or a jump scare.
